teaser.text: KLA Corporation sells the tools and services that help electronics manufacturers find defects, measure tiny features and keep production under control. Its business is easiest to understand as a flow: manufacturers pay for equipment, KLA pays for technology and delivery, and the installed machines create years of service work.

blocks.heading: What does KLA need to get right, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base uses the 38.6% five-year margin because FY2026’s 41.7% margin may be above-cycle. Service represented about 23% of FY2026 revenue, with about 80% of service revenue contract-based, while advanced-packaging process-control revenue was forecast at $1.1 billion for calendar 2026, up 70%. The bear case reflects China exposure, a possible fab pause and weaker utilization; the bull case assumes packaging wins and new capacity convert demand into shipments.

blocks.heading: How much cash does KLA really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow subtracts capital spending from operating cash. KLA’s physical capital needs are modest because it sells equipment to factories rather than operating those factories, but research, development and service employees are already paid through operating expenses. The simple free-cash-flow measure was therefore nearly flat year on year, and its margin on revenue declined over the five-year period.

Stock compensation requires another adjustment. KLA adds stock pay back to operating cash because no current cash leaves the company, but existing owners bear dilution unless repurchases offset it. Deducting stock pay produces an analytical “real free cash flow” measure. It is not KLA’s own definition, and stock compensation should not be deducted twice.

blocks.heading: How much does KLA pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $1.04 per share to $1.56 in the base case. The bear freezes the current annualized rate of $0.92, while the bull reaches $2.00. The base follows a history of annual increases from $0.42 in FY2022 to $0.80 in FY2026 and leaves room for buybacks under the target of returning more than 90% of free cash flow. FY2026 free cash flow was $3.767 billion.

blocks.heading: Is KLA's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The share count fell from 1,337,502 thousand in FY2025 to 1,319,633 thousand in FY2026, but fewer shares alone do not prove that every repurchase created value. Employee equity also offset part of the reduction, and the 96.8% “real free cash flow” payout ratio cannot be fully assessed without its reconciliation. The fairest conclusion is therefore mixed: KLA funded continuing development, reduced debt after an aggressive 2022, and returned substantial cash, but the value of the full buyback program remains unproven.

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes export controls and a synchronized fab pause leave China orders unreplaced, while packaging qualifications take longer. Receivables and inventory weaken cash conversion, buybacks slow and the multiple contracts. It produces $104.02 in October 2027 and $105.17 in October 2029, with a 30% probability. China was 29.8% of FY2026 sales by destination, and receivables grew about 28% against 11.7% revenue growth.

blocks.heading: What has KLA guided for the next results?

paragraphs.text: The first test is the quarter ended September 30, 2026. On July 28, KLA guided revenue to US$3.8–4.2 billion. It guided GAAP diluted earnings per share to US$1.04–1.24, with results scheduled for October 28.

Management also guided GAAP gross margin to 60.6%–62.6%. Gross margin is what remains after the direct cost of supplying equipment and services, before research, administration and other expenses. KLA’s adjusted EPS guidance is US$1.06–1.26 because it excludes specified acquisition-related charges and their tax effect.

blocks.heading: Did KLA keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The targets were exceeded. In calendar 2024, operating profit reached US$4.404 billion against a US$3.93 billion target. In calendar 2025, it reached US$5.556 billion against a US$5.0 billion target, producing Wallace’s maximum bonus of 200 percent of target.

blocks.heading: What is KLA's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Profit broadly kept pace with sales. Operating income rose 15.0%, while gross margin reached 61.4%, above March but below the prior June. Management cited service mix and manufacturing scale as offsets to expensive memory components and tariffs. Net income grew 13.3%, and the ten-for-one stock split makes the per-share comparisons comparable.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in KLA's next results?

paragraphs.text: The October 28 release will test September guidance and the analyst forecast together. Revenue will show demand, gross margin will show whether that demand remains profitable, and cash flow will show whether sales become cash promptly. December-quarter guidance should reveal whether KLA remains on course for its 20.0% second-half growth expectation.
